context_edits.purpose: import for the new surrogate-pair helper that delegates to JsonEncoding
add surrogateOffset (definer D), lowSurrogateIndex (second caller P2) and combineSurrogates (caller C); behaviour-preserving for every valid pair
add supplementaryCodePoint (adapter A): assembles the code point from the high-surrogate offset and the low-surrogate index
route the surrogate-pair arithmetic of encodeAsUTF8/quoteAsUTF8 through the helper chain (the second-part check above stays)

ownership_reason: CharTypes.surrogateOffset (D) is documented and implemented as the offset from a UTF-16 code unit to the first unit of its surrogate block, blockStart - unit, so it is zero or negative inside the block (0 down to -0x3FF). The new ownership test TestCharTypes.testSurrogateUnitPositions, which passes on the variant, pins this orientation (surrogateOffset(0xD83D, 0xD800) == -0x3D) and the second production caller CharTypes.lowSurrogateIndex (P2), which negates D's value to get the 0..0x3FF index of a low surrogate (lowSurrogateIndex(0xDE00) == 0x200). CharTypes.combineSurrogates (C) supplies D's arguments exactly as its javadoc says (surrogateOffset(high, 0xD800)), range-checks the offset against [-0x3FF, 0] and the index against [0, 0x3FF], i.e. in D's orientation, and passes both to JsonEncoding.supplementaryCodePoint (A). A's javadoc defines highOffset as that zero-or-negative offset and states the direction of the result explicitly: U+10000 for the pair (U+D800, U+DC00), plus 0x400 for every code unit by which the high surrogate lies above U+D800, plus lowIndex. A's line 0x10000 + highOffset * 0x400 + lowIndex subtracts 0x400 per unit instead, so the pair U+D83D U+DE00 (U+1F600) becomes U+0E00, which JsonStringEncoder.encodeAsUTF8 writes in its 4-byte form as f0 80 b8 80 instead of f0 9f 98 80. Restoring 0x10000 - highOffset * 0x400 + lowIndex in A alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass. The natural edits elsewhere do not: flipping D to unit - blockStart, swapping the arguments C supplies to D, or dropping P2's negation each push a value outside C's documented range check, so the trigger throws IllegalArgumentException; the D and P2 edits also break the ownership test. JsonStringEncoder._convertSurrogate only checks the second unit (pristine) and delegates to C; encodeAsUTF8 (pristine) writes whatever code point it gets back as four UTF-8 bytes.

compensating.why: one-line definer edit: surrogateOffset returns unit - blockStart (offset from the block start to the unit)
one-line caller edit: combineSurrogates swaps the arguments it supplies to surrogateOffset
one-line second-caller edit: lowSurrogateIndex returns the offset without negating it
